extraction.name: MVBench
extraction.description: A comprehensive multi-modal video understanding benchmark covering 20 challenging video tasks that require temporal understanding and cannot be effectively solved with a single frame. The benchmark systematically transforms static image tasks into dynamic video tasks requiring temporal skills ranging from perception to cognition.
extraction.creator: Kunchang Li, Yali Wang, Yinan He, Yizhuo Li, Yi Wang, Yi Liu, Zun Wang, Jilan Xu, Guo Chen, Ping Luo, Limin Wang, Yu Qiao
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Data was collected from 11 existing public video datasets covering diverse domains and scenes, ranging from first-person to third-person perspectives and indoor to outdoor environments. Videos were filtered based on temporal sensitivity (intermediate duration of 5-35 seconds), video diversity, and question difficulty. Multiple-choice QAs were automatically generated from existing video annotations using ChatGPT and template-based construction methods.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data consists of video clips and annotations from 11 public video datasets: STAR, PAXION, Moments in Time V1, FunQA, CLEVRER, Perception Test, Charades-STA, MoVQA, NTU RGB+D, VLN-CE, and TVQA. These datasets contain videos with ground truth annotations for various temporal understanding tasks including actions, objects, positions, scenes, counts, attributes, poses, characters, and cognitive reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Multiple-choice QA generation using automatic conversion of public video annotations via LLMs. Questions generated by ChatGPT based on task definitions. Answer options constructed via template-based methods (from ground truth annotations) or LLM-based generation. Options randomly sampled (3-5 per question), shuffled, and length-normalized using LLM. System prompt guides MLLMs to scrutinize video content including actions, poses, object details and movements. Answer prompt format 'Best Option: (' ensures reliable option extraction.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: 100% option extraction rate achieved through prompt design. Evaluation uses accuracy metric with ground-truth video annotations to guarantee fairness and avoid biased LLM scoring. Question difficulty balanced by excluding overly simple or complex questions.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 1 multiple-choice QA per video (200 QA pairs per task)
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: ChatGPT for question generation, answer option generation, instruction generation, and text length normalization. LLMs used for converting annotations to multiple-choice format.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark reveals that existing MLLMs are far from satisfactory in temporal understanding. VideoChat2 struggles in position, count, and character tasks, performing less effectively than VideoChat2text, which could be attributed to the lack of exposure to these tasks during instruction tuning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The benchmark is designed to evaluate the temporal understanding capabilities of Multi-modal Large Language Models (MLLMs) through multiple-choice QA tasks covering 20 challenging video tasks. It is used for testing and evaluation purposes to assess comprehension capabilities across various temporal skills ranging from perception to cognition.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: All models and data are available at https://github.com/OpenGVLab/Ask-Anything
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Automatic QA generation paradigm that converts open-sourced video annotations into multiple-choice QAs for evaluating MLLMs

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: we automatically convert the video annotations into this format via LLMs. Specifically, we first use ChatGPT to generate a question for each video, based on the task definition. Then, we create the corresponding answer options as follows. (1) Template-Based Construction: For most questions, we construct the option candidates directly from the ground truth annotations... (2) LLM-Based Generation: For the Unexpected Action task in particular, we leverage ChatGPT for converting open-ended QAs into multiple-choice QA with answer options... For all questions, we randomly sample 3 to 5 answer options from the available candidates, and shuffle the option order... we further use LLM to guarantee that all the answer options of a question are of similar and reasonable lengths.
